title: What Is Recovery Like After Endoscopic Transsphenoidal Surgery?
metaDescription: Learn what to expect during recovery after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery, including hospital stay, nasal care, and managing CSF leaks. Expert tips from Prof. Guive Sharifi.
excerpt: Recovery after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery involves a short hospital stay, careful nasal care, and monitoring for complications like CSF leaks. Here's what to expect.

content.text: Recovery after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery (TSS) typically involves a hospital stay of a few days, followed by careful management at home to ensure healing and avoid complications. Patients usually experience nasal congestion and mild discomfort, but most return to normal activities within weeks. Understanding the recovery process helps you prepare and know what to expect.
Hospital Stay After Endoscopic Transsphenoidal Surgery

After the surgery, you will stay in the hospital for about 2 to 4 days. During this time, doctors monitor your vital signs and watch for any signs of complications such as bleeding or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leaks. Nasal packing or splints may be placed to support healing and reduce bleeding. Pain is usually mild and controlled with medication. Early mobilization is encouraged to prevent blood clots and improve recovery.
Nasal Care and Packing During Recovery

Nasal packing is common after endoscopic TSS to help control bleeding and support the surgical site. This packing is usually removed within a few days after surgery. You may experience nasal congestion, a feeling of fullness, or mild discomfort during this time. It is important to avoid blowing your nose forcefully to prevent damage or CSF leaks. Your surgeon will provide instructions on gentle nasal rinses to keep the area clean and promote healing.
Managing Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) Leak Recovery

A CSF leak can occur if the thin membrane around the brain is opened during surgery. If this happens, your surgeon will take steps to repair it during the operation. After surgery, signs of a CSF leak include clear fluid draining from the nose, headaches, or a salty taste in the mouth. If you notice these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Recovery from a CSF leak may require additional treatment or a longer hospital stay, but many patients heal well with proper care.
Returning to Normal Activities and Follow-Up Care

Most patients can return to light activities within 1 to 2 weeks after surgery. Strenuous exercise, heavy lifting, and bending over should be avoided for at least 4 to 6 weeks to reduce pressure on the surgical site. Follow-up visits with your neurosurgeon are important to monitor healing and hormone levels, as pituitary surgery can affect hormone production. Your doctor will guide you on when it is safe to resume work, driving, and flying.
Frequently Asked Questions About Recovery After Endoscopic Transsphenoidal Surgery
When can I go back to work after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery?

Most patients return to work within 2 to 4 weeks, depending on the type of work and how well they are healing. Desk jobs may allow an earlier return, while physically demanding jobs require more time off. Your surgeon will advise based on your recovery progress.
Is it safe to fly after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery?

Flying is usually safe after 4 to 6 weeks post-surgery, once your surgeon confirms there are no complications like CSF leaks or infections. Air pressure changes can affect healing, so it is important to get medical clearance before traveling by air.
When can I wash my hair after the surgery?

You can typically wash your hair gently 2 to 3 days after surgery, avoiding strong water pressure on the nose or surgical area. Use mild shampoo and avoid scrubbing the nasal area. Your surgeon will provide specific instructions based on your case.
When is it safe to drive after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery?

Driving should be avoided for at least 2 weeks after surgery or until you are no longer taking narcotic pain medications and feel alert. Your surgeon will confirm when it is safe based on your recovery and medication use.
How long does fatigue last after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery?

Fatigue is common for several weeks after surgery as your body heals. Most patients notice improvement by 4 to 6 weeks, but some may feel tired longer. Rest, good nutrition, and gradual return to activity help reduce fatigue.
